law.series: z_t ~ N(0,1) independent; x_t = treatment_loading z_{t-1} + e_t; y_t = beta x_t + confounder_to_outcome z_{t-1} + 0.5 u_t

oracle.method: Closed form of the stated linear structural law: the lag-0 contrast E[y_t | do(x_t = 1)] - E[y_t | do(x_t = 0)] is the structural coefficient beta = 2 whatever the confounder strength, because do(x_t) cuts z_{t-1} -> x_t; adjusting for the confounder recovers it and omitting it converges to beta + gamma a/(a^2 + 1) = 2.3529 for gamma = 0.8, a = 0.6 (the PAG whose graph omits z_{t-1} -> y_t is fitted on the law with gamma = 0). The refuter contract lists the refuters the lag-zero study runs at each depth and inference mode (validation-suite design, not derivable); the placebo treatment and the dummy outcome have the exact null 0, the random common cause, subset and bootstrap refuters the original value as expectation. The e-value passes only through the confidence limit of the effect, so a study without a standard error reports it uninformative and failed (asserted); the prior-predictive verdict depends on the prior scale and is not asserted.
oracle.formula: beta (the structural coefficient of x_t in y_t); unadjusted slope beta + gamma a / (a^2 + 1)
asserted_outputs: effect (within tolerance.effect; the identified-set ends for a class Bayesian study)
refuter_contract.Frequentist and Bayesian (the refuters that run)
refuter_contract.null_expected and original_expected (placebo and stability refuter values)
context_only_outputs: unadjusted_plim (documents what omitting the confounder would give)
oracle.independence_basis: The generator evaluates the stated structural coefficient and the omitted-variable slope in exact rationals; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated linear law.
oracle.historical_exposure: Written for this fixture from the stated law and the declared inputs; no product implementation source was consulted to obtain the values.
